key_insight: DenseNet121 led ten pretrained models in classifying benign versus malignant breast histopathology images, achieving 99.4% test accuracy and 0.999 AUC-ROC.
clinical_relevance: Interpretable image classification could support breast pathology assessment, but clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Benchmarked ten ImageNet-pretrained CNN and transformer models on BreakHis using a patient-level split.
Explained predictions with Grad-CAM, LIME, Integrated Gradients, and LRP.
Explanations highlighted nuclei-rich and glandular regions.
evidence_signal: On the BreakHis test set, DenseNet121 significantly outperformed all other evaluated models (reported p < 0.001).
watch_item: The abstract reports no external or prospective validation, so generalizability to routine clinical settings remains uncertain.
paper_title: Interpretable Deep Learning Models for Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using Medical Imaging
